suspicions.claim: The validation error message for text length still references the old 280-character limit instead of the new 140-character limit
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/posts with JSON body {"text": "x" * 150} and Authorization Bearer token; read response status 400 and response.json.errors[0].message to see if it mentions 280 or 140
suspicions.evidence: Probe probe_s1_text_limit_error_message sent POST /api/posts with 150-char text but both base and head returned 201 (success), not 400, so the validation error message was never observed.

suspicions.claim: The validation error message for text length on post edit still references the old 280-character limit instead of the new 140-character limit
suspicions.trigger: Create a post with text length <= 140, then send PUT /api/posts/<id> with JSON body {"text": "x" * 150} and Authorization Bearer token; read response status 400 and response.json.errors[0].message to see if it mentions 280 or 140
suspicions.evidence: Round2 probe_s2_edit_text_limit_error_message sent PUT /api/posts/151 with 150-char text; base returned 200 while head returned 400 with error message 'Length must be between 1 and 140.' confirming the new limit is enforced on edit.

suspicions.claim: The Post model database column still allows 280 characters while schema validation only allows 140, causing potential database truncation or integrity errors for direct database inserts
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/posts with JSON body {"text": "x" * 140} and Authorization Bearer token; verify response status 201 and response.json.text length is 140; then directly insert a Post with 200-character text via database session to see if it succeeds (bypassing schema validation)
suspicions.evidence: Probes for s3 only tested POST /api/posts with 140-char text (both 201) and POST /api/fake/posts (404); no direct database insert with 200-char text was attempted, so the claim about DB column length is untested.

suspicions.claim: Existing posts with text length between 141-280 characters become invalid under new schema but remain in database, causing validation errors when fetched or paginated
suspicions.trigger: Directly insert a Post with 200-character text via database session, then send GET /api/posts with Authorization Bearer token; read response status and check if validation error occurs during serialization
suspicions.evidence: Probes for s4 attempted to insert a long post via POST /api/fake/posts (404) and GET /api/posts returned 200 both times; no direct DB insert of 200-char text occurred, so validation on fetch is untested.

suspicions.claim: The fake posts CLI command still generates posts with up to 280 characters (fake.paragraph()[:280]) which will fail validation when the app runs with new schema
suspicions.trigger: Run flask fake posts 10 command; then send GET /api/posts with Authorization Bearer token; check if any returned posts have text length > 140 or if validation errors occur
suspicions.evidence: Probes for s5 tried POST /api/fake/posts (404) and GET /api/posts (200 both); the fake posts CLI command was not successfully invoked, so whether it generates >140-char posts is untested.

suspicions.claim: The Post model __repr__ or url property might be affected by text length changes, though unlikely
suspicions.trigger: Create a post with exactly 140 characters, then send GET /api/posts/<id> with Authorization Bearer token; verify response.json.url format and response.json.text length
suspicions.evidence: Probe probe_s6_post_repr_url_140_chars created a 140-char post and GET /api/posts/151 returned 200 with identical responses in base and head, showing no regression in __repr__ or url property.
